question: Which of the following best describes Word2vec? A. A programming language used to build artificial intelligence models. B. A statistical technique used to analyze word frequency in a text corpus. C. A deep learning algorithm used to generate word embeddings from text data. D. A database management system designed for storing and querying word data.
discussion: Selected Answer: C Word2Vec is a neural network based technique developed by Google to learn vector representations (embeddings) of words from large text datasets. Words with similar meanings are placed close to each other in the vector space. It uses architectures such as: CBOW (Continuous Bag of Words) Skip-Gram upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: In the context of language models, what does an autoregressive model predict? A. The probability of the next token in a text given the previous tokens. B. The probability of the next token using a Monte Carlo sampling of past tokens. C. The next token solely using recurrent network or LTSM cells. D. The probability of the next token by looking at the previous and future input tokens.
discussion: Selected Answer: A An autoregressive language model generates text by predicting the next token (word, subword, or character) based on all the tokens that came before it. For example: Input: "The capital of France is" The model predicts the probability distribution for the next token, such as: Paris → 90% Lyon → 5% Marseille → 3% Others → 2% It then selects or samples the next token and repeats the process. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: In large-language models, what is the purpose of the attention mechanism? A. To measure the importance of the words in the output sequence. B. To determine the order in which words are generated. C. To capture the order of the words in the input sequence. D. To assign weights to each word in the input sequence.
discussion: Selected Answer: D The attention mechanism allows a language model to focus on the most relevant parts of the input when processing or generating text. It does this by assigning different weights (attention scores) to input tokens based on their relevance to the current token being processed. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: In the transformer architecture, what is the purpose of positional encoding? A. To remove redundant information from the input sequence. B. To encode the semantic meaning of each token in the input sequence. C. To add information about the order of each token in the input sequence. D. To encode the importance of each token in the input sequence.
discussion: Selected Answer: C Transformers process all tokens in parallel and, by themselves, do not understand the order of words. Positional encoding is added to token embeddings to provide information about the position of each token in the sequence. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

Selected Answer: C In the transformer architecture, positional encoding is essential because, unlike recurrent models, transformers do not process tokens sequentially. Positional encoding provides information about the position of each token in the sequence, allowing the model to capture the order of words. upvoted 2 times Submit Cancel

question: Which technique is designed to train a deep learning model by adjusting the weights of the neural network based on the error between the predicted and actual outputs? A. Gradient Boosting B. Principal Component Analysis C. K-means Clustering D. Backpropagation
discussion: Selected Answer: D Backpropagation is the algorithm used to train neural networks by: Making a prediction (forward pass). Calculating the error between the predicted output and the actual output. Propagating the error backward through the network. Computing gradients for each weight. Updating the weights (typically using Gradient Descent or an optimizer such as Adam) to reduce the error. This process is repeated over many training iterations until the model learns to make accurate predictions. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: Why is layer normalization important in transformer architectures? A. To enhance the model’s ability to generalize to new data. B. To compress the model size for efficient storage. C. To stabilize the learning process by adjusting the inputs across the features. D. To encode positional information within the sequence.
discussion: Selected Answer: C Layer Normalization helps stabilize and speed up the training of Transformer models by normalizing the activations across the features of each token. This keeps values within a consistent range, reducing training instability and helping gradients flow more effectively through deep networks. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: Why do we need positional encoding in transformer-based models? A. To increase the throughput of the model. B. To represent the order of elements in a sequence. C. To prevent overfitting of the model. D. To reduce the dimensionality of the input data.
